datasheet_id_and_revision: SBOS261D, November 2002, revised December 2008 (package addendum dated 11-Nov-2025)
datasheet_status: Production data (pdf p.1 footer); OPA699ID and OPA699IDR Active / Production (addendum, pdf p.25)
scope_note: Headline pass only: tables, front page, noise/open-loop page, limiter theory, compensation, ESD and addendum pages were read; most typical-characteristic and application pages were not read in detail and no curves were digitized.

conventions.src: 'pdf p.N' = 1-based PDF page index; for pdf pages 1-24 the printed page number equals the pdf index.
conventions.types: TYP = typical 25 C; MIN/MAX = guaranteed (temperature stated; test level A = 100% tested at 25 C, B = characterization and simulation, C = typical only); CURVE = read from a plot.
conventions.ec_conditions: +-5 V tables (pdf p.3-4): G = +6, RF = 750 ohm, RL = 500 ohm, VH = -VL = 2 V. +5 V tables (pdf p.5-6): G = +6, RF = 750 ohm, RL = 500 ohm to VCM = 2.5 V, VL = VCM - 1.2 V, VH = VCM + 1.2 V.

compensation: decompensated voltage-feedback, stable for G >= +4 V/V (pdf p.1, p.19); nominal phase margin 60 deg at a gain of +6 / noise gain 6 (pdf p.21)

min_stable_gain.conditions: 'stable for gains >= +4' (pdf p.1); 'gain of +4V/V stable op amp' (pdf p.19); gain peaking 7.5 dB TYP at G = +4 (pdf p.3).
min_stable_gain.what_datasheet_says_below_or_at_min: Inconsistency: pdf p.21 states 'internally compensated to be unity-gain stable' in the same paragraph that gives 60 deg phase margin at a gain of +6, and then recommends the OPA698 if a unity-gain-stable amplifier is needed. Below the minimum gain: 'Low-gain compensation for improved SFDR' (pdf p.16-17, not read in detail) shapes the noise gain with a capacitor from the inverting input to ground and a feedback capacitor (front-page example: G = -2 with RG = 374 ohm, RF = 750 ohm, CS = 18 pF, CF = 4 pF, pdf p.1). For a photodiode TIA with large RF, the inverting-input capacitance causes peaking or oscillation; add a small capacitor in parallel with RF, which sets the bandwidth through the RF-CF pole, or use a T network (pdf p.21).

supply.total_max_V: 12 per the tables (+-6 V / +12 V MAX); text says 13 V maximum total (inconsistent)
supply.src: pdf p.2 (abs max), p.3 and p.5 (operating voltage), p.23 (13 V in text)

phase_margin_or_crossover.value: Open-loop gain and phase plot exists (VO = 0.5 Vpp, +-5 V, pdf p.10) but was not digitized in this headline pass

open_loop_curve.figure: OPEN-LOOP GAIN AND PHASE, pdf p.10

overdrive_recovery.conditions: limited step response recovery time, VIN = +-0.7 V to 0 V step, +-5 V (G = +6, so 4.2 V of drive against 2-V limits); MAX 1.9 ns (25C), 2 ns (0-70C), 2.1 ns (-40-85C), test level B
+5 V, VIN = VCM +-0.4 V to VCM step

overdrive_recovery.value: overshoot entering limit: 250 mV (+-5 V, VIN 0 to +-0.7 V step); 55 mV (+5 V)

output_limiting.mechanism: Two buffered limiter inputs VH (pin 8) and VL (pin 5); when the output tries to exceed them the corresponding limiter buffer takes control of the output (output-side limiting, so accuracy does not change with gain and the internal signal path does not saturate) (pdf p.19).
output_limiting.limit_offset_accuracy: +-10 mV TYP, +-30 mV MAX (25C), +-35 / +-40 mV over temperature (+-5 V); +-15 mV TYP, +-30 MAX (+5 V)
output_limiting.linear_to_within: 30 mV of VH or VL (pdf p.19) [front page says 20 mV, pdf p.1]; linearity guardband 30 mV TYP (5 MHz, 2 Vpp, SFDR -3 dB criterion)
output_limiting.limit_range: VL >= -VS + 0.7 V and VH <= +VS - 0.7 V; VH - VL >= 400 mV (pdf p.19); maximum limit voltage +-4.3 V (+-5 V); output voltage limited range +-3.8 V TYP (+-5 V)
output_limiting.default_limits_pins_open: +-3.5 V TYP, +-3.3 V MIN (25C) at +-5 V; VCM +-1.1 V TYP (+-0.9 MIN) at +5 V
output_limiting.limiter_pin_bias_current: 50 uA TYP magnitude (40 MIN / 60 MAX at 25C), IVH positive (out of pin 8) and IVL negative (into pin 5) at +-5 V; -15 uA at +5 V; limiter input impedance 3.4 Mohm || 1 pF
output_limiting.limiter_ac: limiter small-signal bandwidth 600 MHz (+-5 V) / 450 MHz (+5 V); limiter slew rate 125 / 100 V/us; limiter feedthrough -60 dB at 5 MHz
output_limiting.op_amp_bias_shift: input bias current shifts by 3 uA (+-5 V) / 5 uA (+5 V) between linear and limited operation
output_limiting.setting_guidance: Resistor dividers are fine when limits are more than 2.1 V from the supplies (run >= 1 mA, e.g. 2.5 mA, through the divider and include the 50-uA limiter currents); within 2.1 V of the supplies use low-impedance buffers; bypass pins 5 and 8 (pdf p.20). Distortion is barely affected until the limits are within about +-1.1 V of a +-1 V output (Fig 13, pdf p.20).

voltage_noise.curve_note: INPUT VOLTAGE AND CURRENT NOISE DENSITY plot (pdf p.10) spans 100 Hz to 10 MHz with flat asymptotes labelled 4.1 nV/rtHz and 2 pA/rtHz; not digitized.

current_noise.hf_behavior: flat to 10 MHz (highest plotted); not specified above 10 MHz
current_noise.how_measured_or_defined: single curve; the noise model (Fig 16, pdf p.21) uses IBN and IBI current-noise sources

input_capacitance.definition_notes: Input impedance: differential-mode 0.32 Mohm || 1 pF, common-mode 3.5 Mohm || 1 pF (TYP, both supplies)

input_bias_current.conditions: +-5 V, current positive out of node; MAX +-10 (25C); offset current +-0.3 TYP, +-2 MAX

output_swing.type: TYP (VCM +-1.6 V; MIN VCM +-1.4 V), VH/VL = VCM +-1.8 V

imd_or_oip3.value: about 34-37 dBm from 1 to 20 MHz, falling to about 31 dBm at 50 MHz

packages.name: SO-8 (D, D0008A)
packages.body_mm: 4.81-5.00 x 3.81-3.98, 1.75 mm max height (text layer of outline drawing, pdf p.30)
packages.notes: Only package; OPA699ID (tube 75) and OPA699IDR (reel 2500), MSL 2 / 260C, -40 to 85C (pdf p.2, p.4, p.25).

pinout_notes: 1 NC, 2 IN-, 3 IN+, 4 -VS, 5 VL (lower limit), 6 Output, 7 +VS, 8 VH (upper limit) (pdf p.2).

tia_content.what: Text guidance only: for large RF (photodiode TIA) add a small capacitor across RF; bandwidth then set by the RF-CF pole; or use a T network
Listed application: 'Transimpedance with fast overdrive recovery' (no worked TIA example found in the pages read)

application_guidance: Capacitive loads >= 2 pF need a series output resistor (recommended RS vs CL curve, pdf p.10; Fig 14, pdf p.20-21).
Resistors > 1.5 kohm with about 0.2 pF parasitic add a pole/zero below 500 MHz; 750-ohm RF is the recommended starting point (pdf p.23).
abs_max_and_input_protection: Supply +-6.5 V; input voltage +-VS; differential input +-VS; limiter voltage range +-(VS - 0.7 V); TJ 150C; storage -65 to 125C; ESD HBM 2000 V, MM 200 V, CDM 1000 V (pdf p.2). ESD diodes from every pin to both supplies, typically 30 mA continuous; add series resistors if driven from higher-voltage sources (pdf p.23).
other_notes: Inconsistency: 'unity-gain stable' (pdf p.21) versus 'stable for gains >= +4' (pdf p.1, p.19).
Inconsistency: linear to within 20 mV of the limits (pdf p.1) versus 30 mV (pdf p.19).
Inconsistency: maximum total supply 13 V in text (pdf p.23) versus +-6 V / 12 V in the tables (pdf p.3, p.5).
Schmitt-trigger example propagation delay 4 ns (pdf p.19).
